title: Compute brief - 10 November 2026
description: Public grids are closing their doors while builders bring their own power: Norway paused new data centre grid reservations until as late as August 2027, while SpaceX filed for a $24 billion gas plant and super-compute site at Starbase and PPL agreed terms to build about 2 GW of generation for one QTS campus. Nvidia fell for a second day on a report that $7.5 billion of its hardware reached China through a network tied to the Megaspeed affair. Wire: Norway, PPL and QTS, SpaceX Starbase, EuroHPC gigafactory reset, Equinix SG6, Megaspeed. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The grid says wait. The builders bring their own power.
lede: Norway's grid operator Statnett on Monday paused new grid reservations for data centres until as late as 1 August 2027 and the government said it will license data centres, after requests reached 31 GW in a country whose peak demand is just over 25 GW. Builders are answering queue risk by owning generation: SpaceX filed a hearing notice for a roughly $24 billion gas-fired plant and super-compute facility at Starbase, Texas, and PPL's Invitium agreed terms to build about 2 GW of gas, fuel cells and batteries for a single QTS campus in Pennsylvania, where PPL's advanced pipeline is now 35.3 GW. Nvidia fell for a second day, down nearly 6% by late morning Eastern on Tuesday, after The Information reported at least $7.5 billion of its hardware reached Chinese buyers through a network linked to the Megaspeed executive at the centre of the board's investigation; AMD and Broadcom rose. Europe slipped again: EuroHPC voided every AI gigafactory tender for technical reasons, with large sites now due 3 December and medium sites 4 February. Live list prices held: 70 confirms, 0 ticks and 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.
